chunks.title: Echolocation Biology
chunks.content: Echolocation is biological sonar used by bats and dolphins. Bats emit FM sweeps (100kHz to 25kHz in 2-5ms), process echoes through parallel frequency channels in the cochlea, and reconstruct target range/shape/texture. Dolphins use broadband clicks with increasing rate when approaching targets. Key principles: active sensing (organism generates the signal), parallel channel decomposition, matched filter processing (compare echo against pulse template), adaptive emission (modify calls based on environment).

chunks.title: Echolocation SCAT Computational Model
chunks.content: The SCAT (Spectrogram Correlation and Transformation) model: Stage 1 - Cochlear filterbank (gammatone filters produce time-frequency spectrograms). Stage 2 - Spectrogram Correlation (cross-correlate pulse and echo spectrograms for coarse delay/range). Stage 3 - Spectrogram Transformation (extract fine structure between reflecting points/glints using ALT effects). Stage 4 - Integration across all channels. The DEO optimization algorithm translates echolocation to metaheuristic: exploration phase (random wide pings) then exploitation phase (focused pings around best results).

chunks.title: Echolocation Mae Architecture Mapping
chunks.content: Proposed EcholocationSensor in communication/ or sensing/ module. Agents send structured probe messages (sonar pulses), receive state summaries as echoes, build local system maps. Multiple probe types (health, capability, load, trust) = parallel frequency channels. Adaptive emission rate accelerates when anomalies detected. Integrates with WorldModel, SomaticMap, ThreatDetector, PredictiveField, MycelialSubstrate. Novel capability: detect dark regions - crashed subsystems, network partitions, silent failures that passive monitoring misses.
